contracts: Observed snapshots bind the trusted registry project/worktree identity, actual Git HEAD, complete selected raw hashes and actual sample time.
Capture rechecks mapping/HEAD/all refs before branding. Missing, unsafe, unreadable or incomplete evidence stays unknown with explicit refs; no creation.
Three-year age does not erase knowledge. Matching project/HEAD/raw refs is current as of capture, changes are needs_recheck (stale), missing prior or unequal ref sets are unknown.
Current means byte-reference match, not semantic truth. Owner and progress are not inferred.
Trusted Host acceptance binds exact proposal, complete history-prefix digest, tip ID/content hash, project/HEAD/raw refs, command exit and stdout hash.
Freshness module checks the Host attestation, re-observes before/after its callback and before append, rejects source/mapping drift and structurally forged receipts.

Append validates every old revision, preserves all JSON content/hash/metadata with immutable independent copies, and rejects prefix drift, malformed histories, duplicate acceptance IDs and receipt replay.
Superseded is represented by an explicit receipt-bound supersedesRevisionId on the appended replacement; old revisions are retained unchanged.
No time-to-live, decay, automatic deletion, Native memory writer, new fact database, model or shell execution engine.

limitations: Evidence paths must be approved by a trusted Host. Literal private/runtime exclusions are not a general secret-content classifier or OS sandbox.
Host must actually execute verification and verify its accepted history. A matching callback JSON does not independently prove that execution happened.
The module checks the supplied complete-history digest/tip and consumes one in-process receipt. Cross-process atomic persistence/CAS belongs to the Host; this module only returns an append proposal.
Only live module-minted observations and receipts can authorize; serialized history/prior snapshots are untrusted experience leads.
